_comment: Verifies reaction_diffusion pitfall 4 on scikit-fem 12.0.1 (2026-08-06). Schnakenberg on 16x16 ElementQuad1 (289 DOFs), a=0.1 b=0.9 gamma=1000, dt=2e-3, 40 backward-Euler steps, identical seed and 1e-2 perturbation in every run. d_v/d_u = 1 decays to 8.9e-16, = 8 to 1.1e-03, = 10 patterns at 9.8e-01, = 40 patterns at 4.1e+00, so the mechanism switches on between 8 and 10. That brackets the analytic threshold the fixture computes from the dispersion relation, d_crit = 8.5676 (root of (d*f_u+g_v)^2 = 4*d*det), which makes the claim's quoted '~10' a safe rule of thumb rather than the exact number. At equal diffusivities the first Turing condition already fails (d*f_u+g_v = -0.2) and the largest growth rate over all Neumann modes is -100, versus +31 and +411 at d_v = 40. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 sets D_V_WRONG, the equal diffusivity d_v = d_u = 1, to the shipped D_V_RIGHT = 40 -- the documented fix (fast inhibitor, slow activator). Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 15 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 switches the Turing mechanism back on in the wrong variant and removes 'equal_diffusivity_fails_turing_condition=True', 'lambda_max_at_equal_diffusivity_lt_0=True' and 'equal_diffusivity_spread_lt_1e_8=True', so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
